samples.summary: `dispose()`'s neuter cannot stop the in-flight clipboard paste it claims to close — `EditorAPI.paste()` resumes after `await navigator.clipboard.read()` and writes through the disposed TextEditor
samples.evidence: The new doc comment on `isDisposed` and the comment inside `dispose()` name "a clipboard read" as the case disposal revokes. But neutering replaces `api.paste` only for *future* calls; a call already suspended at `await navigator.clipboard.read()` (editor.ts:3979) resumes in its own closure and reaches `textEditor.pasteContent({ html, text })` (editor.ts:3997, and the `readText()` fallback at 4005). `textEditor` is a `const` (editor.ts:2503) that `dispose()` never nulls — it only calls `textEditor?.dispose()` — and `TextEditor.pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659) checks `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting` but NOT `this.disposed`, unlike the other two resuming writes which do (`deferPaste`, text-editor.ts:1609; `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:4261, whose comment even asserts "this is the only one that resumes"). Consequence in exactly the scenario the delta describes: an `editor`→`viewer` downgrade on `/shared/:token` disposes this editor and remounts a read-only one over the SAME Yorkie document (docs-view.tsx:565/590), so the stale paste lands CRDT content into the document a viewer is now supposed to only read, and into a document the disposed editor no longer renders. Fix: check `this.disposed` in `pasteContent`, or re-check a captured `disposed` flag after each await in `api.paste`.

samples.summary: Disposal-based revocation is incomplete: `getStore()`/`getDoc()` still hand out live writable handles after `dispose()`, so a stale holder can write around `MUTATING_METHODS`
samples.evidence: `dispose()` now asserts "a write from a stale holder must not land" and "every mutating method has been neutered", and `isDisposed`'s doc says a disposed editor "is inert". Neither holds for the two accessors that return live handles: under `readOnly` they are backed by `readOnlyDocStore` (the split is documented at editor.ts:4505), but under disposal nothing wraps them — `getStore: () => (readOnly ? readStore : pageSetupGuardedStore)` and `getDoc: () => doc` are untouched by `neuterMutations`. Writes through those handles bypass the allowlist entirely: `docs-find-bar.tsx:65-68` captures `editor.getDoc()` and `editor.getStore().snapshot()` into `FindReplaceState`, and `handleReplace`/`handleReplaceAll` (docs-find-bar.tsx:132-148) mutate the Doc directly — its own comment at line 26-32 states this path is *not* covered by `MUTATING_METHODS`. That path happens to be saved today only by the separate `readOnly` prop gate at line 134/143, which is a different mechanism from disposal; any holder of `getStore()`/`getDoc()` that resumes after an await has no such gate. I could not point at a confirmed in-tree async caller, hence medium confidence, but the invariant the delta introduces is not actually enforced.

samples.summary: `canUndo()` latch misdiagnoses a rebuilt/removed floor entry as "dropped" whenever the stack is at the cap, permanently disabling the undo floor
samples.evidence: When the identity lookup misses, the code disambiguates purely on `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (line 3062): "Only a stack at the cap can have dropped anything, which is what tells the two apart." That is not exhaustive — a stack *at the cap* can also have had the floor entry rebuilt or removed for reasons other than shifting (e.g. the SDK transforming/pruning undo entries after a remote change, which is normal in a collaborative doc). In that case the code takes the permissive branch and latches `undoFloorMark = null; undoFloorDepth = 0; undoFloorIdentityUsable = false`, so `canUndo()` returns true unconditionally from then on (line 3045) until the next `setDocument()`. The floor exists precisely because "Yorkie's CRDT redo of writeFullDocument can conflict with subsequent text insertions" and undoing past it "would destroy blocks the cursor still references" (lines 663-667, 910-912) — i.e. the misdiagnosis fails in the data-destroying direction, and it fails permanently. The <cap branch deliberately degrades to the safe depth fallback; the at-cap branch does the opposite with no independent evidence that a shift actually occurred (e.g. no comparison against a previously observed floor index, which is already cached in `undoFloorDepth` and would distinguish the two).

samples.summary: The `isDisposed()` branch fires on any ordinary unmount, showing "this document is no longer editable" to a user who merely navigated away (and in dev on every StrictMode remount)
samples.evidence: `editor.isDisposed()` is true for every disposal, not just a permission downgrade: the docs effect disposes on unmount and on any change of `[didMount, doc, readOnly]` (docs-view.tsx:565, 590), and `main.tsx:16` wraps the app in `StrictMode`, whose dev mount/unmount/mount sequence disposes the first editor. An upload in flight across any of those resolves into `toast.error("Image not inserted: this document is no longer editable")` — a factually wrong message (the document is still editable; the surface went away) raised from a torn-down surface. Same at line 195 for `insertImageFromUrl`. Distinguishing "disposed" from "disposed because write authority was lost" would need a reason, or the message should be neutral.

samples.summary: `editor.isDisposed()` is called unguarded on an `EditorAPI`-shaped object; any implementation lacking the new member throws, and the throw is swallowed into a bogus "Image upload failed" toast after a successful upload
samples.evidence: `isDisposed` is a brand-new required `EditorAPI` member and `insertImageFromFile` calls it directly inside the `try`. `packages/frontend` has no `tsc`, and `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:100-114` documents exactly this hazard for the last new member added — test doubles and other holders are built with `as unknown as EditorAPI`, so a *new* member reached at runtime is feature-detected there (`typeof editor.hasCopiedFormat === "function"`). Here there is no such detection: an object without `isDisposed` raises `TypeError`, which the surrounding `catch` converts into `toast.error("Image upload failed: ...")` — after the upload already succeeded, so the user is told the upload failed, nothing is inserted, and the uploaded object is orphaned. Only `fakeEditor` in image-insert.test.ts was updated; other frontend doubles passed to these helpers (or any future one) hit this silently.

samples.summary: On the disposed path the already-uploaded image is left orphaned on the server with no cleanup or logging
samples.evidence: `if (editor.isDisposed()) { toast.error(...); return; }` returns after `await upload(file)` has already persisted the file to workspace storage, and nothing deletes it or records the id. Same shape as the pre-existing error paths, so contained, but the new early return adds one more source of unreferenced blobs.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out. editor.ts:3974-4007 `paste()` guards only `if (!textEditor) return` before `await navigator.clipboard.read()` (3979) and then calls `textEditor.pasteContent(...)` (3997, and the readText fallback at 4005) with no post-await disposal re-check. `dispose()` (4434-4444) sets `disposed = true` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, which only reassigns `api[name] = noop` (1061-1067) — future calls only; a suspended closure holds its captured `textEditor` (`const` at 2503, never nulled, only `textEditor?.dispose()` at 4454). `TextEditor.pasteContent` (text-editor.ts:1659-1668) checks `this.readOnly` and `this.pasting` but not `this.disposed`, and `TextEditor.dispose()` (6068-6094) sets `disposed` without setting `readOnly`, so neither existing guard fires. The two sibling resuming writes do check it (`deferPaste` 1609; `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` 4261). The path is reachable in normal use: docs-context-menu.tsx:272 invokes `editor!.paste()`, and docs-view.tsx:565/590 disposes and remounts a read-only editor over the same Yorkie doc on an editor→viewer downgrade (comment at 585-588). YorkieDocStore.dispose() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:689-693) only unsubscribes and does not block writes, so the stale paste mutates the shared document; any throw would be swallowed by the catch at editor.ts:4001/4006. Major impact: CRDT content written into a document a viewer should only read and which the disposed editor no longer renders.

I could not refute on 'already-guarded': the only thing standing between a stale handle and a write is the separate `readOnly` prop check at docs-find-bar.tsx:134/143 (a different mechanism from disposal) plus the absence of a current async writer — not a guard on the disposal path. That is not exhaustive — a stack *at the cap* can also have had the floor entry rebuilt or removed for reasons other than shifting (e.g. the SDK transforming/pruning undo entries after a remote change, which is normal in a collaborative doc). In that case the code takes the permissive branch and latches `undoFloorMark = null; undoFloorDepth = 0; undoFloorIdentityUsable = false`, so `canUndo()` returns true unconditionally from then on (line 3045) until the next `setDocument()`. The floor exists precisely because "Yorkie's CRDT redo of writeFullDocument can conflict with subsequent text insertions" and undoing past it "would destroy blocks the cursor still references" (lines 663-667, 910-912) — i.e. the misdiagnosis fails in the data-destroying direction, and it fails permanently. The <cap branch deliberately degrades to the safe depth fallback; the at-cap branch does the opposite with no independent evidence that a shift actually occurred (e.g. no comparison against a previously observed floor index, which is already cached in `undoFloorDepth` and would distinguish the two).

verdict.reason: The described code is present verbatim: canUndo() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3043-3076) disambiguates an identity-lookup miss solely on `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (line 3062) and, on that branch, latches undoFloorMark=null/undoFloorDepth=0/undoFloorIdentityUsable=false (3067-3069). Combined with the short-circuit at line 3045, the floor is then permanently disabled until markUndoFloor() re-arms (constructor line 668 or setDocument line 914), and undo() (3029-3034) has no other gate, so the failure direction is data-destroying per the invariant at lines 663-667/910-912. The heuristic is genuinely non-exhaustive: the `< cap` fall-through (3072-3074) acknowledges "rebuilt in place" as a real state, yet the identical condition at or above the cap is classified as "dropped". The mark-time identity check (927-933) only rules out a copying accessor at mark time and does not guard against later rebuild/prune, so it is not an existing guard for this case. I could not construct a counterexample proving a miss at cap always implies a shift: @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.20 is not vendored (no node_modules in the tree), and the constant's own comment (562-569) concedes cap drift, which for a larger real cap opens a length-50-to-real-cap window where no shift can have occurred yet. Existing tests (tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:371-392, 401-421) cover only the genuine-shift and copying-accessor cases, not rebuilt-at-cap. In-lane (logic/boundary/broken invariant), not refutable on any named ground.

finding.summary: Undo floor now depends on reference identity of an SDK test-accessor's return value
finding.evidence: `canUndo()` was rewritten from a depth comparison to `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, where `stack` comes from `this.doc.getUndoStackForTest()`. This is only correct if that accessor returns the *live* internal array whose element identities are stable across calls. If the SDK returns a fresh/copied array of entries (or ever rebuilds an entry, e.g. during change transformation on remote merge), `lastIndexOf` yields -1 and `canUndo()` becomes unconditionally true — the initial-load floor disappears and a user can undo past `setDocument`, which the surrounding comment says 'would destroy blocks the cursor still references'. I could not verify the SDK behaviour: `node_modules` is not present in this checkout and only `docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md:58` describes the accessor ('arrays of reverse-op batches'). Worth confirming against @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.8 before relying on identity.

verdict.reason: The finding claims canUndo() is `stack.lastIndexOf(this.undoFloorMark) < stack.length - 1`, so a copying/rebuilding accessor yields -1 and canUndo() becomes unconditionally true, erasing the initial-load floor. The code does not behave that way. (a) At mark time, markUndoFloor() (yorkie-doc-store.ts:923-934) reads getUndoStackForTest() twice and only sets undoFloorIdentityUsable when the top entry is the same object across reads (931-933); canUndo() gates the entire identity branch on that flag (3047). So a copying/entry-rebuilding accessor disables the identity path and leaves undoFloorDepth (set to the full stack length at 925) enforcing the floor — the safe, pre-existing behaviour. (b) Even inside the identity branch, a -1 result does not return true unconditionally: `if (index >= 0)` (3052) handles the found case, and the not-found case returns true only when `stack.length >= YORKIE_MAX_UNDO_DEPTH` (3062-3071); otherwise it falls through to the conservative `return stack.length > this.undoFloorDepth;` (3075). markUndoFloor() has only two call sites (668, 914) and canUndo() is the sole consumer of the mark (undo() at 3029-3031 routes through it), so no path bypasses these guards.
